title: A competitive market for juice: consumer and producer surplus, then a rise in costs
scenario: The market for bottles of fresh juice in Corlin, an invented city, has many sellers and many buyers. Demand is a straight line that reaches zero at \$12 a bottle, supply is a straight line that starts at \$2 a bottle, and the market is in equilibrium at \$6 with 400 bottles sold a day.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Calculate consumer surplus at the equilibrium. Show your work.

rubric.point: \$1,200, with work: one half times 400 times (\$12 − \$6)

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Shade the area that represents producer surplus at the equilibrium.

slips.cs: That area is under demand and above the price: consumer surplus. Producer surplus is above supply and below the price.

rubric.point: Shades the area above supply and below the equilibrium price, out to the equilibrium quantity
accept: the triangle above S below PE

parts.sample: Producer surplus is the triangle above the supply curve and below the equilibrium price, from zero out to the equilibrium quantity.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: A disease damages fruit orchards, and the price of fruit used to make juice rises. Show the effect on the market for juice and the new equilibrium on a correctly drawn graph.

key.because: a rise in the price of an input (fruit)

slips.D: Fruit is an input for juice makers, so its price shifts supply, not demand.

rubric.point: The new equilibrium shows a higher price and a smaller quantity, marked on the axes
accept: P2 above P1 and Q2 below Q1

parts.sample: The higher fruit price raises the cost of each bottle, so supply shifts left from S1 to S2. S2 crosses demand at a higher price, P2, and a smaller quantity, Q2, marked with dashed lines to the axes.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Based on your answer to part C, identify what happens to consumer surplus, and explain.

rubric.point: Consumer surplus decreases, because buyers pay a higher price and buy fewer bottles (the triangle under demand above the price shrinks)
accept: falls because the price rises and quantity falls

parts.sample: Consumer surplus decreases. Buyers now pay a higher price and buy fewer bottles, so the triangle under demand and above the price is smaller.
